newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kinkel sees continued outside presence in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel sees continued outside presence in Bosnia.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Sunday that the view was growing that an international presence would be needed in Bosnia after the end of the year.
"In Bosnia, you don't have self-supported stability so the civil implementation of the Dayton agreements will have to be safeguarded from the outside," he told reporters.
"The view is growing that the institutions concerned (with Bosnia) -- the United Nations, NATO, the Europeans -- will decide that such outside help would be necessary," he said.
"I don't have the impression that the Europeans or the Germans would shy from participation," Kinkel added.
EU foreign ministers at a weekend meeting in the Irish town of Tralee endorsed the idea of a two-year peace consolidation period in Bosnia.
The mandate of a NATO-led IFOR peace force expires in December. Elections are to be held in the country on September 14.
International Bosnia mediator Carl Bildt told reporters there was wide support for the idea of holding elections again two years from now in September 1998.
